observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher explains steps methodically with verbal counts and repetition. He breaks down combinations slowly and drills them multiple times before connecting them.

lesson_structure.note: Teacher introduces the Samoan slap dance (Fa'ataupati).
First step breakdown with jumps and stomps.
Second step breakdown hitting legs and chest.

extraction.counting_scheme: 1-2-3-4 / lualua tongi e / a'a tongi e
safety: Make sure your in a good stance like your on a horse
Keep your back straight and bent down

steps_taught.name: First Step (Lualua tongi e)
steps_taught.counts: lualua tongi e / e a'a tongi e
steps_taught.description: Stomp and clap combo while jumping right and left.

steps_taught.name: Second Step
steps_taught.description: Jump and hit legs, chest, sides, and swing down.

what_works: Repeating sequences multiple times before moving on
what_hinders: Fast transitions between detailed explanations and full speed demonstrations

quotes.text: teach you young boys how to do the fa'ataupati
make sure you're in a good stance like this, like you're on a horse
when I say ready, you say sa'o'i
That's the first step, very easy to do.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher demonstrates squat stance with straight back and hands on hips, turning to the side to show posture.
Teacher performs stomping and clapping sequence while facing front.

extraction.distinctive_method: Integrating traditional Samoan vocal cues and call-and-response phrases directly into the physical drills.
